name: Battlezone Auxiliary Math Box PCB
drawing: DP-156 sheet 3 Side B, section of 035678-01
coverage: All five blocks on DP-156 sheet 3 Side B read: Math Box, Output Latch, Audio Output, Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator, Power Input. Cross-checked device for device against the Figure 1 test-point map on sheet 1 Side B, which is what caught E1 and D1 being missed on the first pass. Passives are recorded only where they set a rate, a level or an adjustment.

B1.note: Atari 036174; 32x8 entry PROM, A0-A4 from EAB0-4, D0-D7 drive the microcode PROM address bus; enabled by BEGIN

C1.note: microcode address latch A0-A7, clocked by D5 (A6A3), output enable from BEGIN

F1.note: Atari 036180; microcode PROM, highest microcode field

K2.note: Atari-marked Am2901 4-bit slice, DIP-40; least significant slice

H/J2.note: Atari-marked Am2901 4-bit slice, DIP-40; spans H2 and J2

D/E2.note: Atari-marked Am2901 4-bit slice, DIP-40; spans D2 and E2, most significant slice

C5.note: A12 latched by CLK; produces STOP, cleared by BEGIN

C3.note: both halves used; one decodes EAB5/EAB6 to SWITCHES, the other EAB3/EAB4 to YHI and YLO

C4.note: ER/WB and EPHI2 gating into M START

D3.note: E3MHZ gating; also in the ALU carry path with E5

D4.note: M START, CLK and STOP gating

D5.note: A16 and CLK to A6A3, the C1 latch clock

E3.note: open-collector, EDB7 pulled up by R2 (1k)

E4.note: inverters through the clock and start logic

E5.note: XOR in the ALU carry path

M2.note: latches EDB0-7 into MOTOR EN, SOUND ENABLE, ENGINE REV EN, SHELL L/S, SHELL EN, EXPLO L/S and EXPLO EN -- every sound enable on the board comes from this one chip

B/C2.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator
B/C2.note: POKEY, DIP-40, spans B2 and C2; P0-P7 read the control panel switches directly, D0-D7 on EDB, AUD out through R36/C25

H5.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator
H5.note: shift register in the noise generator, fed back through two E5 XOR gates; cleared by SOUND ENABLE

F3.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator
F3.note: engine-rev timer; R10 (100k), R11 (250k pot) and C11 set the rate

F4.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator
F4.note: motor sound divider, held by MOTOR EN

F5.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator
F5.note: second motor sound divider, held by MOTOR EN

J5.section: Control Panel Inputs and Audio Generator

L4.note: quad analog switch gating shell, explosion and engine paths

J3.note: quad analog switch, shell and explosion envelope charge/discharge into C9 and C14

K5.note: quad op-amp on +22V: shell and explosion shapers, engine shaper, and the summing amp that drives AUD+

M5.note: inverts the mix to give AUD-, so the board puts out a differential pair on edge pins 5 and 6 with AUD RETURN on E

CR2.note: +5V present indicator through R37 (150R). Same designator as the game PCB LED but a different board -- do not confuse the two

E1.note: low half of the microcode program counter; QA-QD (pins 14,13,12,11) drive PROM address A0-A3, carry out on 15 into D1. Loaded from B1 via LD, clocked by CLK

D1.note: high half of the microcode program counter; QA-QD (pins 14,13,12,11) drive PROM address A4-A7. Loaded from B1 via LD -- B1 supplies the entry address, E1/D1 then step through the microcode

interconnect.note: Circled numbers on this sheet are interconnect-connector pins, not test points -- the drawing's own legend says a square is an edge connector, a circle an interconnect connector, and a rounded shape a test point.

signatures.note: Four-digit alphanumeric codes on this sheet are signature-analysis signatures of Math Box test points, in the HP analyser alphabet (0-9 A C F H P U). Unboxed codes are taken during Test #1; boxed ones during the test named on the box. The 2nd printing adds that any code marked with an asterisk is taken with a 1k pull-up between the analyser data probe and +5V -- without that resistor those readings will not reproduce.

B1_address.note: pins 14,13,12,11,10 = A4..A0. Values from the typeset Figure 2A on sheet 1 Side B, which is legible where the hand-lettered boxes on sheet 3 Side B are not.

B1_data.test: Test #2A on the 2nd printing, Test #2B on the 1st

prom_address_test2b.note: Confirmed against the typeset Figure 2B on sheet 1 Side B, which gives them per device pin: D1 pins 11,12,13,14 = 92F3, A856, 3050, H8F9 (address A7..A4) and E1 pins 11,12,13,14 = 9569, 3U53, 9F47, 4FUF (address A3..A0). That matches the 2nd printing of sheet 3 Side B exactly and settles the reversal.

alu.note: signatures printed under the four 137004-001 slices; asterisked ones need the 1k pull-up

edb_test3.note: Figure 3 on sheet 1 Side B gives these per device pin: H/J2 pins 22,23,24,25 = 1441, 2883, 5107, A20P and E/D2 pins 22,23,24,25 = 4414, 883A, 1074, 20P9. The hand-lettered box on sheet 3 Side B reads the fifth as 441H rather than 4414; the typeset figure is the better source but the two do disagree.

notes: Sheet 3 Side B is a DIFFERENT PCB from sheets 2 and 3 Side A. Those are sections of the game PCB 035742; this is the Auxiliary PCB 035678-01. The designator grids are separate, so C1 here is not the C1 on the game PCB and the two must never be merged into one board map.

The Math Box is a microcoded bit-slice machine, not a fixed-function circuit: four 137004-001 slices (Atari-marked Am2901) at K2, F2, H/J2 and D/E2 make a 16-bit ALU, sequenced by six 82S129 microcode PROMs at M1, L1, K1, J1, H1 and F1 carrying Atari parts 036175 to 036180 in that order, with an 82S123 at B1 (036174) providing the entry address and C1 (LS374) latching it.
This is the PCB Red Baron shares with Battlezone, so every device position and signature here applies to both games. A known-good board from either checks the other.

The 2nd printing (Rev B) is the more useful document: it adds signal-flow arrows for each signature test, the ORIGIN markers, the asterisk/1k pull-up note, and the R11 tank-idle adjustment procedure. The 1st printing (Rev A) has none of these.

The POKEY (B/C2) lives on this board, not the game PCB, and it reads the control panel switches on its own P0-P7 lines. So the control panel goes through the POKEY while the coin door goes through an LS244 on the game PCB -- two completely different paths for what looks like the same kind of input.

Sound splits in two at the mixer: shell, explosion and engine are generated on this board by the 4066 switches, the 555 and the LS161 dividers, and are summed into K5 through R25, R28 and R26. Everything else -- radar blip, bump, saucer, saucer disintegrate, missile, bonus and the 1812 Overture -- arrives as one signal from the POKEY through R27. Silence on one group but not the other says which half to look at.

Audio leaves as a differential pair: K5 drives AUD+ and M5 inverts it for AUD-, on edge pins 5 and 6 with AUD RETURN on E. The output stage runs on +22V, which the board takes in directly on pin 3/X -- so a board with working logic and no sound may simply be missing +22V.
This PCB has its own +5V LED at CR2 through R37, the same arrangement as the game PCB. Two boards, two power LEDs, both called CR2.

Sheet 1 Side B is the key to this board: it carries the whole signature analysis procedure plus four typeset figures giving signatures per device pin. Those figures are far more legible than the hand-lettered boxes on sheet 3 Side B, and every disagreement between the two printings of sheet 3 Side B is settled by them.

The sequencer is now complete end to end: B1 (82S123, entry PROM) supplies a start address, E1 and D1 (two LS161s) latch it and then step, their eight outputs address the six 82S129 microcode PROMs M1 through F1, and those drive the four 137004-001 slices. A Math Box that starts but does not finish, versus one that never starts, separates at E1/D1 against B1.
conflicts: Figure 3 on sheet 1 Side B gives E/D2 pin 22 as 4414; the Test #3 box on sheet 3 Side B gives the same net as 441H. Both are valid signature strings and both are legible. The typeset figure is the more reliable of the two, but this one is not settled.
corrections: The LS245-style note about what the earlier signature record said needed correcting itself. The published note listed Math Box device positions as 'L1, K1, J1, H1, F1, E1, D1, C1, J2, F/H2, E2, C/D2, K3, J3, J4, H4, D3, D4, D5, C3'. It never claimed those were the microcode PROMs, and an earlier version of this file said it did -- that was unfair to it. What is actually wrong with the list is narrower: it omits M1, and it gives the four ALU slices as J2, F/H2, E2 and C/D2 where the drawings say K2, F2, H/J2 and D/E2. Figure 1 on sheet 1 Side B, which is the test-point map the list was derived from, shows M1 through F1 for the PROMs and K2, H/J2, F2, E/D2 for the slices.
'CAPE' is not a possible signature, because E is not in the analyser's alphabet (0-9 A C F H P U). The code is C4P5, read from the typeset Figure 2A.

adjustments.R11: 250k potentiometer near the centre of the Auxiliary PCB, setting the engine/tank idle rate through the F3 555. The 2nd printing prints the procedure: in play mode the idle should be moderately paced, neither stalling nor racing, and driving the tank forward should raise it. Replacing this PCB means readjusting R11.

control_panel.note: each switch line goes through a 1k series resistor into a 0.1uF shunt with a 470R pull-up, so an intermittent control can be a failed filter capacitor rather than a failed switch

resolved: RESOLVED. The 1st/2nd printing disagreement over the Test #2B box at the PROM address pins is settled by Figure 2B on sheet 1 Side B, which gives the same signatures against individual device pins rather than as a column: D1 pins 11-14 carry 92F3, A856, 3050, H8F9 and E1 pins 11-14 carry 9569, 3U53, 9F47, 4FUF. That is the 2nd printing's order. The 1st printing of sheet 3 Side B prints the column reversed, and it is simply wrong.

RESOLVED. 1F47/9F47, 3UF3/3U53 and 4569/9569 are all settled by Figures 2A and 2B, which are typeset rather than hand-lettered: 9F47, 3U53, 9569. The 1st printing of sheet 3 Side B is the odd one out on all three.
RESOLVED. B1's fifth Test #2A code is 2P61, not 2P41 -- typeset in Figure 2A and matching the 2nd printing of sheet 3 Side B. Two independent sources against one.

RESOLVED, and against my own earlier reading. The code at B1 pin 13 is C4P5, not CAP5. Reading the hand-lettered sheet 3 Side B it looked like 'CAPE', and I reasoned from the analyser's alphabet that E was impossible and the character must be a 5, giving CAP5. The alphabet argument was right about the last character and wrong about the third: the typeset Figure 2A prints C4P5. A constraint can tell you a reading is impossible without telling you what the right one is.

signature_procedure.board: Auxiliary PCB 035678-01 (shared by Battlezone and Red Baron)
signature_procedure.source: DP-156 sheet 1 Side B, 'Auxiliary PCB Signature Analysis Procedure'
signature_procedure.equipment: Atari CAT (Computer-Assisted Troubleshooter), Kurz-Kasch Signature II, or HP 5004A signature analyser. Note on the drawing: of two Kurz-Kasch Signature IIs tried, different START, STOP and CLOCK settings were required -- note your own settings while testing a known-good board.
signature_procedure.harness: Atari P/N A036836-01, or make one: Molex 7-circuit housing 09-05-7071 x1, 12-circuit housing 09-50-7121 x3, terminals 08-50-0106 x18, three jumper wires with hook connectors on each end, and a 1k-1.5k quarter-watt pull-up resistor.
signature_procedure.setup: Set the Battlezone self-test switch ON; after about three seconds the monitor should show the self-test pattern. Then jumper a 1k resistor between the two test points on the Analog Vector-Generator PCB to ground five times, or until the video display is blank.

tests.1: Plug the harness Test #1 connector onto the SA header on the Auxiliary PCB. Jumper pin 1 of IC B6 on the Analog Vector-Generator PCB to ground -- this holds RESET to the microprocessor. Verify by probing the +5V test point: it must read CC34. Then probe per Figure 1. The 1k-1.5k resistor runs from +5V on the Auxiliary PCB to the probe tip for this test.
tests.2A: Remove the resistor from the probe, plug the Test #2 connector, remove the jumper from pin 1 of B6, verify at the +5V test point, then probe per Figure 2A.
tests.2B: Test #2 connector still plugged; remove the jumper from pin 6 of B6 on the Analog Vector-Generator PCB, verify a signature of 72A2, then probe per Figure 2B.
tests.3: Plug the Test #3 connector, remove the jumper from pin 6 of B6, verify, then probe per Figure 3.

signature_procedure.isolating: Find the failing test point on sheet 3 Side B and identify the IC the signature is output from, then check all of that IC's inputs. If every input is correct, the IC is the fault -- but first pull the PCB and check the traces common to that pin, top and bottom, for a short to another trace. If an input is wrong, move to the IC sourcing that input and repeat, working upstream until the failing IC is isolated.
signature_procedure.caveat: The verification signatures quoted here for tests 2A, 2B and 3 were read from a scan and only 72A2 and the Test #1 CC34 were confirmed at high magnification. Read the sheet before relying on the others.
